events.summary: Navy assigned 16 disaster response teams to assist flood-affected residents.
Renovation is underway on 25 to 30 official residences returned by former MPs.
Emergency repairs and sandbag reinforcement were carried out near Maruthankerny Bridge.
Flood-affected crop growers to receive compensation of up to LKR 40,000 per acre.
Japan handed over donated equipment valued at US$8.4 million at Katunayake Airport.
Deputy Minister said steps would be taken to build a new Vattuvakal Bridge.
Heavy vehicles were temporarily barred from crossing the flood-damaged bridge.
Government considered compensating farmers for additional crops damaged by heavy rain.
Committees monitored ongoing flood relief work in Northern and Eastern provinces.
Relief for farmers affected by heavy rains was promised after assessments.
Officials arranged medical services and distributed food and essential supplies to displaced people.
Navy relief teams were deployed in three flood-affected districts.
President directed officials to allocate funds for relief to weather-affected communities.
Officials discussed emergency relief and preparedness measures for flood-affected Mannar residents.
Police established a 24-hour centre to coordinate urgent disaster reports and response.
Kalmunai Municipal Council directed private education centres to suspend tuition for two days.
Disaster officials arranged heavy-vehicle transport to take students to examination centres.
Passenger trains between Badulla and Colombo were suspended due to landslides and debris.
Rail service between Badulla and Bandarawela was disrupted by landslides and falling rocks.
Muslim schools in the Eastern Province were closed for two days due to severe weather.
Authorities deployed emergency measures, shelters, food aid and water pumping to respond to flooding.
Farmer organisations and the Agrarian Development Department began repairing a breached tank bund.
Irrigation officials and the army placed sandbags and fencing to protect the tank bund.
IMF staff reached a third-review agreement; the fourth tranche awaits board approval and prior actions.
Western Province plans short-term development of Kakkaithivu beach under the Clean Sri Lanka programme.
The ministry plans an urgent programme to address challenges facing lower-ranking police officers.
Sri Lanka and China signed a supplementary agreement for 1,996 low-income and senior artists’ homes.
UNDP-supported programme handed 61 computers and other technology equipment to national unity officers.
Minister said a Cabinet paper would seek approval to import 70,000 tonnes of rice from India.
Ministry announced fuel-efficient vehicles would be provided to all Members of Parliament.
Education ministry will review prior reforms before proposing new reforms aligned with government policy.
Agriculture ministry established a special unit to address crop damage caused by harmful animals.
Northern Governor approved appointing senior teachers as teacher resource personnel.
Jaffna district officials directed cooked meals for people sheltering in temporary accommodation.
President pledged a public-sector salary increase in the next budget.
President pledged an increase in Aswesuma benefits in the next budget.
China handed Northern Province’s governor a cheque for residents’ livelihood support.
Government decided to import 70,000 tonnes of local rice to address a market shortage.
Government announced payments for low-income students’ school books and supplies, starting next year.
ADB approved a $200 million loan to strengthen Sri Lanka’s public financial sector.
First phase paid fertilizer subsidies to 129,229 farmers for the Maha season.
Railways operated extra trains on several routes after the election and long weekend.
Dutch representatives agreed to provide technical and financial support for Sri Lankan sector programmes.
Extra buses and trains operated to help voters travel for the general election.
Seventy extra buses operated in Colombo, Gampaha and Kalutara; 80 more were assigned for Colombo.
Special ferry trips were arranged between Kurikattuwan and Neduntheevu for election day.
Officials arranged special election-day ferry services between Kurikadduwan and Neduntheevu.
First Maha-season fertilizer subsidy payment was deposited for 9,064 Kilinochchi farmers.
International election observers began monitoring duties after meeting Election Commission officials.
Talaimannar-Colombo train service was scheduled to resume after railway development work.
Election Commission introduced online access to voter cards for the parliamentary election.
Disaster Management Centre implemented a five-day response plan for election-related emergencies.
University Grants Commission decided to close universities on November 13 and 14 for the election.
Police announced election security deployment and post-election patrols nationwide.
Police restricted Matara coastal road traffic for ballot transport and election security.
Officials were instructed to grant election leave to university staff and students.
China's disaster compensation assistance was sent to the Treasury.
Additional budget funds were allocated to rebuild disaster-damaged homes.
The Treasury released funds to the Defence Ministry for disaster recovery.
China's promised emergency goods will be distributed after receipt and accounting.
Health Ministry announced nationwide measles vaccination activities would begin.
Government ordered schools closed for the general election on November 13 and 14.
Cabinet approved awarding Vitol Asia the 92-octane petrol supply tender.
President directed ministers to live in their own districts and end official Colombo residences.
Government relaxed restrictions on non-religious community events at Galle Face Green.
Officials reported monthly Galle Face management and maintenance costs starting at Rs. 2.5 million.
Cabinet approved contracts for three batches of China-funded low-income housing.
Regulator directed CEB to submit a new tariff reduction proposal by November 8.
Immigration Department announced online appointment booking for passports, effective November 6.
Ministerial secretary appointed a 10-member committee to investigate Aswesuma beneficiary selection complaints.
Vehicle number plate distribution was temporarily suspended over delayed payment to the printing company.
Vehicle owners were temporarily permitted to display their registration numbers on paper.
Postal workers continued distributing official voter cards for the general election.
Postal Department designated November 3 for special delivery of general-election voter cards.
A foreign supplier delivered 50,000 blank passports under an awarded procurement contract.
Procurement began for another batch of blank passports.
EU election observers began monitoring Sri Lanka’s general election.
